- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% if recent price is falling.  
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); apply “cool-down” correction: subtract 0.5–1.5% per day for 3–7 days post-spike.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70–75), model often holds too high; reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until reversion completes.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overestimate early in the horizon (first 5–7 days); apply linear decay: reduce forecast by 0.5–1% per day for first 7 days.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often misjudges direction; align forecast with sentiment trend only if sentiment is consistent for 3+ days.
